summary: Iteration 17 e2e testing: Digital Audit Workbook (backend /api/audit/* + UI), AML reminder exclusivity fix, Settings mobile layout fix, and non-audit engagement regression. 21/21 new pytest cases pass; iteration_16 regression suite (4 tests) still passes. UI flows all pass end-to-end (start audit, 25-section sidebar, yes/no + text + underscore sub-question saves, flag on 'No', file upload, Excel/PDF export, Mark Complete, Start New Period with roll-forward, tab hidden for non-audit types). Two data-quality/UX defects found in the parsed audit template (duplicate question code B19 causing shared state + React duplicate-key error; is_input heuristic never marks label rows).

minor.issue: Duplicate question code 'B19' in section 2 (LEGAL DOCUMENTS): 'System generated B/s & P&L match with the audited financial statements' and 'Additional Comments:' both parse to code B19. Both share one responses.B19 document key, so answering one auto-answers the other and progress is double-counted (2 of 35 done from a single answer). parse_template() must de-duplicate codes (e.g. append _1/_2 suffix on collision).

is_input heuristic in audit_workbook.parse_template() never fires: 295 of 295 rows are is_input=True, so pure label/header rows are rendered as answerable questions (e.g. 'Additional Comments:', A8_1 'Auditor'). Inflates the denominator and shows meaningless input rows.

ui_bugs.issue: React console error 'Encountered two children with the same key' in Legal Documents section, caused by the duplicate B19 template code (key={q.code}); both rows render and mirror the same value.

Minor UX/race: openStartForm() renders the start form immediately and fetches client audit history afterwards, so the 'Roll Forward Static Data From' dropdown pops in ~1-2s late (an automated/quick user can submit before it appears). Suggest loading history before showing the form or rendering a disabled placeholder select.

design_issues.screen: Audit Workbook - roll forward / history dropdowns
issues: Roll-forward and history <select> option labels list every prior audit including duplicates with identical period text ('TEST FY 2025-26 (completed)' x3 in test data) - no client/created-date disambiguation, hard to pick the right prior year once multiple audits exist per client.

action_items: De-duplicate question codes in audit_workbook.parse_template() (B19 collision in section 2) so each row has a unique responses key; re-seed audit_templates (bump TEMPLATE_ID/version since seed is skipped when the doc exists).
Fix the is_input/label detection heuristic so header/label rows ('Additional Comments:', 'Auditor') are not counted as answerable questions.
Optional: fetch client audit history before rendering the start form so the roll-forward dropdown is present on first paint.
critical_code_review_comments: audit_workbook.seed_audit_template() early-returns when a template with TEMPLATE_ID exists, so any parser fix will NOT take effect on existing environments - version the template_id or add a re-seed/migration path.

server.py save_audit_response builds $set paths from the URL {code}; codes are validated against the template (good) but keep enforcing that guard - any future code containing '.' or '$' would corrupt the document. Verified underscore codes (A8_1, B1_1) work end-to-end.
server.py is ~3577 lines - well over the 700-line guideline; the audit routes are a good candidate for extraction into an APIRouter module.
Audit export/download endpoints accept a session token via the ?auth= query param (verified working). Tokens in URLs land in logs/history - consider a short-lived signed download token.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all flows pass; 1 duplicate-key React error, 1 dropdown load race)

rca_of_the_issue: Duplicate code B19: parse_template() reuses the Sl.No value from the source XLS as the unique question code, and the Legal Documents sheet repeats '19' on two rows ('System generated B/s & P&L match...' and 'Additional Comments:'). Because responses are stored keyed by code, both rows read/write responses.B19 - answering one visually answers both and compute_progress counts 2 completions for a single answer; React also logs a duplicate-key error since AuditQuestionRow uses key={q.code}. Fix: detect code collisions during parsing and suffix them, then re-seed with a new template version. Related: the is_label heuristic (requires no code AND no remarks AND ALL-UPPERCASE text) never matches real rows, so every one of the 295 rows is answerable.
